dialogue.speaker: mtangazaji
dialogue.text: Good afternoon and welcome to your Weekly Rangeland and Climate Advisory. I am your host, Fatuma Hassan, broadcasting from Marsabit Community Radio. In studio with me today is Dr. Peter Leruk, our County Senior Livestock and Agricultural Officer. Dr. Leruk, a warm welcome to the studio.

dialogue.speaker: mtaalamu
dialogue.text: Thank you, Fatuma. It is a pleasure to be here with our pastoralists, herders, and livestock traders tuning in across Laisamis and neighbouring areas.

dialogue.speaker: mtangazaji
dialogue.text: Dr. Leruk, looking at the latest satellite moisture and precipitation reports, what should our communities expect over the next two weeks?

dialogue.speaker: mtaalamu
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, no rainfall is projected for the coming fourteen days. Dry winds and strong daytime heat will persist. Consequently, pasture cover across southern Laisamis has deteriorated significantly.

dialogue.speaker: mtangazaji
dialogue.text: That is critical guidance for our migration planning. What is the latest verified status on our key community water points?

dialogue.speaker: mtaalamu
dialogue.text: We have confirmed that Kargi Pan has completely dried up, so herders must avoid driving herds towards that corridor. However, the primary Laisamis Town borehole remains operational with safe, dependable yield.

dialogue.speaker: mtangazaji
dialogue.text: What vital advice do you have regarding livestock health and local market trends?

dialogue.speaker: mtaalamu
dialogue.text: First, vaccinate your small stock against contagious respiratory disease before moving them north. Second, goat prices are softening at the local market, so herders are strongly encouraged to de-stock weaker animals now to preserve household income.

dialogue.speaker: mtangazaji
dialogue.text: Thank you very much, Dr. Peter Leruk, for these timely insights. I am Fatuma Hassan, wishing all our pastoralist families safe grazing until our next bulletin.
